attributes.axis_log: Single axis, one probe: REGRESSED real 46->86, and the instruction count moved AWAY from target (106->110 against a target of 108) with the multiset going 4t->6t. The failure signature is the law's documented TAX exactly: a whole extra symbol materialization appeared deep in the function (+1 lis at @0xf0 and +3 addi), because the member form makes MWCC re-materialize potionicon_tab per region while the target caches it once in r31 and merely re-ADDS the index. Reverted; the axis is measured-dead in this spelling.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association.20260831.v1 APPLIED, and its explicit PROCEDURE decided this function: 'count the target's lis/addi pairs for the symbol. If target has one cached base AND per-access adds, the residual is rematerialize-vs-cache register allocation - classify REGISTER_ONLY, record, and move on.' Counted: the target has exactly ONE potionicon_tab lis/addi pair (+0x18/+0x20) AND per-access adds (+0x24, +0x44, the loop's +0xfc, +0x168). That is precisely the not-reachable-by-respelling case, and the measurement below confirms it. claim.law.IG_local-alias-of-a-global-root-pays-the-direct-global-tax.20260901.v1 APPLIED - caching PT(i) in the local `p` pays the direct-global tax. claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges.20260831.v1 screened, consistent.
attributes.probed_form: REVERTED: deleted `Player* players = gPlayerRecords;`, rewrote `players[i].state = 1;` to `PT(i)->state = 1;`, `p = &players[i];` to `p = PT(i);`, and inside the j-loop `Player* other = &players[j];` to `Player* other = PT(j);`. All other lines unchanged.
attributes.residual: REGISTER/SYMBOL-class, named. Target base r31=potionicon_tab and r30=i*0x335C stay live and are re-added at +0x24 and +0x168; r29 becomes PT(i) via `addi r29,r29,3136`. Our base is gPlayers, so every record displacement differs by 0xC40 and the two re-add instructions have no counterpart, which is the whole T108/O106 count gap. IMPORTANT SCOPING NOTE for the next lane: this is NOT the same thing as the TU header's blanket BSS-POOLING GATE claim, which is separately refuted (see claim.law.PL_bss-pooling-gate-is-per-function-not-tu-wide.20260901.v1). activate_player's target genuinely uses potionicon_tab; change_player's and load_player's targets genuinely use gPlayers. Only the potionicon_tab group is affected, and for this function the respelling cure is measured harmful.
